output_json.patch_notes:
Source fix (ContextAssetRequestHandler.handleAssetRequest): after `rootContextResource.forFile(path.resourcePath)` resolves and normalizes the path, the same `illegal` pattern is now matched against `resource.getPath()`; if it matches, the handler returns false without streaming. This is the minimal change that closes the bypass while preserving normal asset serving (legitimate paths that do not resolve into WEB-INF/META-INF/.tml are unaffected).

Regression test (ContextAssetRequestHandlerTest): added `ensure_traversal_assets_are_rejected` with a DataProvider of traversal payloads (e.g. `foo/../WEB-INF/web.xml`, `a/b/../../WEB-INF/classes/hibernate.cfg.xml`, `x/../META-INF/MANIFEST.MF`, `assets/../Index.tml`). It uses an in-test `AlwaysExistingResource` (a real AbstractResource subclass so the vulnerable forFile normalization is exercised, but which always reports exists()=true) and a `RecordingResourceStreamer` that would return true and record any streamed resource. The test asserts the handler returns false AND that nothing was streamed. Verified this test fails (3 failures) when the source fix is reverted and passes (8/8) with the fix, making it a genuine regression guard.

Verification: POV `bash .security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh` now prints `handleAssetRequest returned: false` / `streamed resource path: null` and exits 1 (was exit 0 / VULNERABLE before). Targeted TestNG run of ContextAssetRequestHandlerTest: 8 tests, 0 failures.

output_json.risk_notes:
Low risk. The change only adds a rejection path (returns false) for asset requests whose normalized path resolves into a protected WEB-INF/META-INF/.tml location — these should never be served as context assets, so no legitimate asset serving is affected. `resource.getPath()` returns the normalized path already used for lookup, so the check is consistent with what would be streamed. forFile() can throw IllegalStateException for paths that escape above root; that pre-existing behavior is unchanged (it surfaces as a request error rather than serving a file), which is acceptable for a malformed/malicious request.

Note on regression_commands: the project drives tests via a TestNG suite XML (src/test/conf/testng.xml), so Gradle's `--tests`/`-Dtest.single` filters do not select individual classes. The provided command compiles then runs the single test class directly via TestNG using the module's compiled classes and Gradle's cached dependency jars (paths under /root/.gradle inside the project container). The full suite (`./gradlew --no-daemon :tapestry-core:test`) also exercises this test but pulls in slow Selenium integration tests.
output_json.summary: Fixed a CWE-022 path traversal / access-control bypass in ContextAssetRequestHandler. The `illegal` regex (blocking WEB-INF, META-INF, and .tml) was only applied to the raw, un-normalized asset path, so a request like `<checksum>/x/../WEB-INF/web.xml` slipped past the guard; AbstractResource.forFile() then normalized the `..` segments to `WEB-INF/web.xml` and streamed the protected descriptor. The patch resolves the Resource first, then re-applies the same `illegal` check to the normalized `resource.getPath()` before streaming, so any path that resolves into a protected folder is rejected.
